tldr: Evening batch: OpenAI publishes three major posts — tracing GPT-5's goblin output quirk origins, detailing Stargate compute infrastructure for AGI, and issuing a five-part cybersecurity action plan. HuggingFace releases a full technical timeline of the OpenAI rogue model intrusion. OpenAI claims GPT-5.6 Sol beats Opus 5 on ARC-AGI-3 but only via its own API test harness, not the official environment. Alibaba open-sources Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-Edit (20B), GLM 5.2 weights are live, and GLM 5.2 gets vision via a Baseten/Kimi encoder merge. Dario Amodei clarifies Anthropic doesn't support open-weight bans but proposes export controls and safety testing. Microsoft ships MAI-Cyber-1, Agent Governance Toolkit, and plans a unified Copilot super app. Hermes Agent integrates Buzz workspace, Garry Tan open-sources GBrain, Nvidia forms an AI security alliance, and Etched closes $300M at $10.3B for transformer ASICs. Community builds TurboFieldfare — running Gemma 4 26B in 2GB RAM on any M-series Mac.

articles.title: Where the Goblins Came From — Tracing GPT-5's Personality Quirks
articles.summary: OpenAI traces the origin of 'goblin' outputs in GPT-5 — timeline, root cause, and fixes for personality-driven behavior quirks.

articles.title: Building the Compute Infrastructure for the Intelligence Age

articles.summary: OpenAI outlines a five-part plan democratizing AI-powered cyber defense and protecting critical infrastructure.

articles.title: OpenAI Claims GPT-5.6 Sol Beats Opus 5 on ARC-AGI-3 — With Caveats

articles.title: China's Open-Weight AI Push — Industrial Policy, Not Altruism

articles.summary: Microsoft's MAI-Cyber-1-Flash powers a new agentic cybersecurity system with zero-trust agent governance.

articles.summary: Open-source toolkit for policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, and execution sandboxing for autonomous AI agents across any framework.
